text:
Both responses capture the key points: the new features, the improvements and fixes, and the v1 connector shutdown moved to 31 January 2027. Now to check accuracy and word count.

Accuracy: The original says "Only about 8 per cent of customers still use v1, so most of you won't need to do anything." Both respond accurately. Response A says "Only ~8% of customers are affected", which is fine. Response B says "No action is needed for most customers" and "about 8% of customers", which is also accurate.

Response A says "Action required (if applicable)" and "The shutdown was extended to 31 January 2027, but switch soon." Accurate. It says the guide is in the help centre. Good. It omits that updates roll out automatically overnight, though it labels the features "(automatic)", which is slightly loose, since that applies to the whole release.

Response B includes "Updates roll out automatically overnight". It states "moved from 30 Nov to 31 Jan 2027", which is precise. It omits the guide in the help centre and the menu path for finding v1. For a manager, the menu path is useful for identifying whether they're affected, but is minor. Response B also omits "staff could be paid late", saying only "timesheets will stop reaching payroll". That consequence is a meaningful omission, though the stoppage itself is covered.

Word counts: A is roughly 115 words, B roughly 120. Let me count B more carefully.

B: "ShiftNest 12.4 (released 28 Oct 2026)" 6; "Updates roll out automatically overnight. No action is needed for most customers." 12 → 18; "New:" 1 → 19; bullets: "Managers can approve shift swaps only for their own areas." 10 → 29; "Public holiday penalty rates now apply automatically for Hospitality and Retail awards, by state." 14 → 43; "Staff get push notifications for open shifts." 7 → 50; "Improvements: Faster roster loading for large sites, unpaid break minutes in timesheet exports, and availability can be set 12 weeks ahead." 22 → 72; "Fixes: Daylight saving hour errors on overnight shifts and South Australia time zone display." 14 → 86; "Action required (only if you use the v1 payroll connector, about 8% of customers): Switch to v2 (about 15 minutes) or timesheets will stop reaching payroll." ~27 → 113; "The shutdown was moved from 30 Nov to 31 Jan 2027, but switching soon is still advised." 16 → 129. So B is likely about 129 words, which is over 120.

A: Heading 6; "Action required (if applicable):" 4 → 10; "If your payroll export uses the old v1 connector (Admin > Integrations > Payroll (v1)), switch to v2." ~16 → 26 (counting symbols maybe more); "The shutdown was extended to 31 January 2027, but switch soon." 10 → 36; "Otherwise timesheets will stop reaching payroll and staff could be paid late." 12 → 48; "It takes about 15 minutes, with a guide in the help centre." 12 → 60; "Only ~8% of customers are affected." 6 → 66; "New features (automatic):" 3 → 69; bullets 9+14+7 = 30 → 99; "Also: faster rosters ... errors." ~28 → 127. Also over 120, maybe, depending on counting. Both near the limit; A is about 127, B about 129. Roughly equal, both marginally over.

Given similar length, A retains the "paid late" consequence and the help guide; B has the "automatic overnight" note and the original date. A's "(automatic)" attaches slightly misleadingly but is harmless. A is slightly better on the key content.

Verdict: A
